instructions: Enforce the working rules in CLAUDE.md. Favor the smallest correct change; flag speculative abstractions and reinvented stdlib. The core library and the service layer are separate concerns and must stay that way.

files.description: Authoritative working rules: layer separation, determinism contract, code-citation requirement, hard-vs-soft constraint separation.

rules.rule: Pure library. Must NOT import from rivet_service, touch a database, read environment variables, make network calls, or reference users/orgs/plans/billing. Flag any such import, or any user_id/org_id threaded into the generator.

Determinism is a contract: no set() iteration, dict-ordering assumptions, hash() of a string, or unordered parallelism in the search/scoring/ordering path or anything downstream of it. Any change to search, scoring, or ordering must come with a test that runs the same request in two subprocesses and compares output bytes.

Building-code minimums are HARD constraints and belong in a validator that rejects a layout, never in the soft penalty score. Any dimensional value taken from a building code must carry a source comment naming the code and clause (e.g. TNCDBR 2019 Rule 52). Flag hardcoded code-derived dimensions with no citation, and any invented code value.
Public functions need type hints. New modules need tests in the same change. Every schema change goes through an Alembic migration -- no manual DDL, no create_all() outside test fixtures.
Frontend reaches the backend only through the API client (lib/api.ts); never embed secrets in client code. Keep SEO metadata (title/description/canonical/OG) intact on marketing routes.
